The overall change that the Chinese have brought to the AI world is beginning to make its mark. Last week, this newsletter talked about Qwen 2.8 27B and how that changes the game. This week it is GLM-5.3-Flash. Both

Running Chinese models, either locally or through services like OpenRouter, is much cheaper than using Claude or ChatGPT. ¶ The results are in. For example on Vercel, more users are now accessing tokens from open-source AI models.

It is, as if for the first,
the Chinese AI companies are now ahead of the US tech giants in the AI race.

Of course, the race itself is far from over. And given that OpenAI and Anthropic have sort of gone silent about their next models, we do not clearly know what they have in store. ¶ The silence can indicate two things: either OpenAI and Anthropic are recalibrating their entire AI strategy in the face of competition and price pressure from Zhipu, MoonShot and Alibaba. Or they have the next-gen AI models that are so good, something Sam Altman hinted at, that releasing them in public would be giving up on the advantage they hold. Irrespective, until OpenAI and Anthropic reveal their hands,
it is safe to say that the Chinese are now no longer behind. They are right up there with the best that the US companies are putting out.
